title: permission-audit-annotator-and-kms-multi-region-fence
author: Elena Torres
description:
Summary: Add a permission-aware audit annotator and a lightweight KMS multi-region fence to enforce region pinning during cryptographic operations. This PR introduces a short-lived middleware in the request flow that annotates audit events with the effective permission delta (what changed compared to the caller's base role) and verifies the KMS key used for encryption/decryption is eligible for the tenant's configured geozone. Motivation: Customers operating under regional data residency rules and strict audit requirements asked for clearer permission provenance in audit logs and stronger enforcement when keys are selected by routing/fallback logic. The annotator helps post-hoc forensics and alerting, while the KMS fence prevents accidental use of a key outside the tenant's permitted set.

Design and scope: - PermissionAuditAnnotator (rbac/audit): inspects PDP decision + request context and emits four new audit fields: auth.principal_id, auth.principal_role, auth.effective_permissions_delta, audit.permission_change_kind (added/removed/unchanged). The annotator runs immediately after PDP returns to avoid changing decision latency profile. - KMSRegionFence (kms/fence): a policy evaluator consulted by the kms-allocator. It is a fast allow/deny check that compares resolved key.location (region tag) against tenant.residency.allowed_geozones. If key fails check, the allocator falls back to an explicitly configured regional keyset; if none available, request is denied with 4xx and logged as policy_denied.kms_region. - Config: new tenant flag residency.enforce_kms_region (false by default) and a fallback keyset pointer residency.kms_fallback_keyset to preserve availability. - Observability: add two new metrics: audit.annotator.latency_ms and kms.fence.denied_count and a structured log field audit.context.permission_delta for use in Console queries. - Backwards compatibility: the annotator is additive (no contract changes to API). The KMS fence is opt-in per tenant to avoid breaking existing customers. A rollout will start with internal tenants and opt-in beta customers.

Commits summary: - 7 commits, authored by E. Torres and pair-reviewed by S. Li: 1) Introduce PermissionAuditAnnotator and tests 2) Wire annotator into auth pipeline 3) Add KMSRegionFence and allocator integration 4) Tenant config + migration guidance 5) Metrics and log schema 6) Integration tests (simulated multi-region tenant) 7) Docs and examples for console + linear references

Files changed (high level): - rbac/audit/annotator.go (new) - rbac/audit/annotator_test.go (new) - kms/fence/fence.go (new) - kms/allocator/allocator.go (updated) - config/tenants_schema.json (updated) - observability/metrics_registry.go (updated) - docs/ops/residency-kms-fence.md (new) - integration-tests/residency/kms-fence-smoketest.yaml (new)

Small snippet (annotator extraction logic): "func extractPermissionDelta(base Role, granted []Permission) string { /* compute added/removed */ }" - kept intentionally short here; full code in rbac/audit/annotator.go.

Testing: - Unit: 24 new unit tests for annotator edge cases (service accounts, delegated operator tokens, empty-role) - Integration: simulated allocator behavior across 3 regions using the test harness; validated fallback and denial paths - CI: full test matrix (linux/go1.20, lint, fmt). Several flaky integration tests were stabilized by tightening timeouts.

CI status: initial run: fail (integration timeout) -> fix timeout in allocator tests -> re-run: pass for unit/lint/format, flaky integration rerun passed. Final merge occurred after green CI and two approvals.

Review conversation (highlights): - S. Li (reviewer): "Can the annotator be a no-op for very hot code paths to guarantee latency SLOs?" Elena: "We intentionally run right after PDP to avoid latency in tokenization/generation phases. Added an adaptive fast-path: if request.token_count > 4096 and tenant.analytics.low_sensitivity == true, annotator tags 'skipped_for_latency' instead of full delta. See annotator.go:fastpath comment." - M. O'Connor (security): "What about cross-tenant operator leases — could an operator grant cause a delta that's misleading?" Elena: "We added operator.origin to the audit context and a cross-check in extractPermissionDelta to detect leases; when present we mark permission_change_kind='operator_elevated' and include lease_id in auth.trace." - R. Gupta (SRE): "If KMS denies a request due to missing fallback keyset, what's our incident escalation path?" Elena: "Denies are recorded as policy_denied.kms_region with tenant_id and request_id. The allocator emits metrics and an alert rule was added to SLO/alerting for >1% denies over 5m for production tenants. Docs include runbook playbook.")

Release notes: "Add permission provenance annotations to audit logs and an opt-in KMS multi-region fence to enforce residency constraints. See docs/residency-kms-fence.md for configuration and migration steps."

Rollout plan: feature flag -> internal tenants -> beta customers -> GA after 3 weeks of metrics review. Merge method: squash and merge.
